subhero.p_2: L’Dor Vador is shaped by the combined experience of its founders, Hannah Berkeley Cohen and Cornelis Greiwe, who together have led more than 100 group journeys in destinations including Cuba and Suriname. Our approach draws on backgrounds in journalism, bespoke travel, and more than three decades of combined experience in special-interest tourism.
subhero.p_3: We share a passion for exploring historical and cultural complexities, as well as connecting people, places, and events to reveal the larger story. These pillars shape every journey we create.

bio.p_2: Hannah Berkeley Cohen is an Ohio native who has called the Caribbean home since 2012. After spending a semester abroad at the University of Havana, she moved to Cuba to document the country’s youth culture, the everyday life of the Cuban middle class, and the island’s dwindling Jewish community. bio.p_3: based in Havana, reporting on American foreign policy toward Cuba, the death of Fidel Castro, and the historic visits of President Obama and the Pope. In Havana, she met with dozens of groups organized by the JDC (American Jewish Joint Distribution Committee), synagogues across North America, and Jewish individuals returning for the first time to Cuba since their parents or grandparents left half a century earlier.
bio.p_4: Reporting for major media outlets gave Hannah rare access to Cuba’s layered society; in 2015, the ease in regulations for travel for Americans to Cuba allowed Hannah to share her insight of the island, with the goal of showcasing a nuanced Cuba: beyond rum, cigars, colorful buildings, and classic cars.

From meetings with ambassadors to conversations with black-market money exchangers, and culinary workshops with Michelin-starred chefs to cozy cooking lessons with grandmothers in modest home kitchens, Cuba Rising offered intimate cultural exchanges with people from all ranks of Cuban society. Each trip was highly customized, with group sizes capped at eight to ensure flexibility and depth of experience. Hannah is fluent in English and Spanish.
bio.p_8: Using her experience in Cuba, Hannah moved to Curaçao in 2024 to delve deeper into the Jewish history and heritage of the island, and create culturally-relevant programs for North American travelers.

Cornelis Greiwe was born in the Netherlands, and lived in Yugoslavia, Greece, Cuba, all before he was 10 years old. He brings more than 20 years of entrepreneurial and leadership experience in the international tourism industry. Throughout his career, he has developed travel products, strengthened regional connectivity in collaboration with airlines, and managed hospitality projects across multiple markets. 

His work is driven by a passion for creating meaningful experiences that bring people, cultures, and networks together. While managing his tour company in Havana, Cornelis also created and produced HAVANA PLAY, a groundbreaking series of electronic music events that gave emerging Cuban DJs and producers a platform to connect with the international electronic music community. During its year-long run, HAVANA PLAY became the most attended weekly music event in Cuba.

After living and working in Cuba and Suriname, Cornelis fell in love with Curaçao and recognized both the importance of tourism to a small island economy and the potential of cultural tourism to contribute to a more sustainable future for the industry. Inspired by the island’s extraordinary cultural richness and layered heritage, he chose to build his life and work in Curaçao, creating thoughtful, culture-forward itineraries that allow visitors to engage more deeply with the island and its people.

Cornelis is fluent in English, Dutch, Spanish, and German.
